ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and Regulations; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46 (Part XII.2); Business Corporations Act (Québec), CQLR c S-31.1 (register of individuals having significant control); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Act), SC 2017, c 21; Charter of the French Language (Québec), CQLR c C-11; applicable FINTRAC Guidance on beneficial ownership, political exposure, and sanctions compliance.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — private internal register: the Register of Individuals with Significant Control is maintained in the corporation's records and is not displayed in the public extract of the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; disclosure to FINTRAC, Revenu Québec, the Registraire, and law enforcement is mandatory upon lawful demand; note the federal CBCA path now operates a corporate beneficial ownership registry under Bill C-42 workflows.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passport bio-pages and proof of residence for each director, officer, and individual with significant control (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec notary or, for foreign documents, the competent ministry of foreign affairs/consulate of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention — in force for Canada since 11 January 2024: Global Affairs Canada (federal documents) and Ministère de la Justice du Québec (Quebec notarized documents); Consular Legalization for non-Hague destination states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / certificate of good conduct of each UBO (required only where enhanced due diligence is triggered by PEP, sanctions, or risk signals)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National, state, or local police fingerprint authority of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, together with a certified translation into French if not issued in French or English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft notarized Register of Individuals with Significant Control (registre des personnes ayant un contrôle significatif) and, if applicable, certificate of corporate status/register of shareholders of the foreign parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec notary/law firm for the register; foreign corporate registry or parent company for the status/shareholder certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for documents originating outside Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-closing screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against: (i) FINTRAC PEP determination (head-of-state, cabinet-level, senior officials, military flag officers, senior executives of state-owned enterprises, and their family/close associates), (ii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) Canadian regulations under SEMA and the Sergei Magnitsky Act, (iv) OFAC SDN List and US 50% Rule where US persons or USD clearing are involved, (v) adverse-media and watchlist databases; enhanced due diligence must include source-of-funds verification and senior-management sign-off for any PEP or medium/high-risk finding; results must be preserved in the corporation's AML/CFT file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Répertoire des entreprises / services.registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca (federal alternative: Corporations Canada NUANS name search and online filing via ised-isde.canada.ca if a CBCA federal corporation is preferred)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (Québec), CQLR c C-11 and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, the name of a Quebec business corporation must be French (the French appellation is the official name); a non-French version may be used only if the French version is registered first; any character set other than roman script must be transliterated phonetically into roman characters; the name must be distinctive, not confusingly similar to existing names or trademarks registered in the REQ database, and must not suggest a legal form inconsistent with a business corporation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banking and deposit tokens: 'Banque', 'Bank', 'Fiducie', 'Trust' — prior authorization of the Autorité des marchés financiers or OSFI required
Insurance/general guarantee tokens: 'Assurance', 'Insurance', 'Mutuelle' — prior authorization required
Professional title tokens: 'Avocat', 'Notaire', 'Comptable', 'Ingénieur', 'Médecin', 'Architecte' — prohibited unless the corporation holds the corresponding professional permit
Government/pseudogovernmental tokens: 'Canada', 'Québec', 'Municipal', 'Commission', 'Ministère', 'Royal', 'Reine' — prohibited unless ministerial/Queen's approval is granted
Education tokens: 'Université', 'Collège', 'École' — subject to prior ministerial authorization
Securities/capital-market tokens: 'Bourse', 'Dépôt', 'Clearing' — subject to AMF authorization
Structural suffixes: 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', 'Ltée' must be used in accordance with the Business Corporations Act (Québec) and may not mislead as to the entity's liability type
Words contrary to public order or public morality, or likely to mislead the public as to the nature of the enterprise

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, including sections 5–10 (constitution and articles), 105–110 (directors), and 119–121 (officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), within the Ministère de l’Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form RE-200), filed with the REQ; the resulting certificate of constitution confirms incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital or minimum paid-up capital applies. Shares are issued for consideration authorized by the board and recorded in the corporation’s securities register. No statutory escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the corporation accept the subscriptions set out in the subscription agreements presented to the directors and issue the corresponding shares upon receipt of the applicable consideration; that the registered office be established at [Quebec street address]; and that [name] be appointed President, [name] Secretary, and [name] Treasurer, each to serve until a successor is appointed or earlier resignation or removal. The officers are authorized to execute documents and take necessary steps to give effect to these resolutions. The Secretary shall enter the subscriptions, share issuances, appointments, and registered-office particulars in the corporation’s books and registers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Select the provincial incorporation route and corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), online services through the Québec government portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm Quebec incorporation is intended, select a compliant corporate name or request a numbered corporation, and check name availability and Quebec language requirements. File the Articles of Incorporation (Form RE-200) electronically or in the accepted paper format. Provide the registered office address, share structure, and required director and incorporator particulars. Sign as prescribed; notarization is generally not required for the standard filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered-corporation request
Payment of the applicable REQ fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For a name objection or filing deficiency, respond to the REQ notice, amend the name or articles, and resubmit the corrected filing with any required fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the certificate of constitution and Quebec enterprise number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After acceptance, retrieve the certificate of constitution and Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). Verify the registered name, date of constitution, address, directors, and filed share provisions. File any required initial declaration of registration within the applicable deadline; confirm whether the incorporation filing completed the registration requirements for the corporation.
required_dossiers: Initial declaration of registration, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inaccurate enterprise-register information through the applicable REQ amendment or declaration filing; retain proof of timely submission and respond to any REQ follow-up.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete organizational proceedings and corporate records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation’s board of directors and registered-office records custodian
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first directors’ meeting or execute written resolutions as permitted. Approve share subscriptions and issuances, adopt the registered office, appoint officers, authorize banking, and approve the fiscal year-end. Record share ownership, directors, officers, and resolutions in the corporate books. Assess beneficial-ownership disclosure duties and file required updates with the REQ.
required_dossiers: Share subscription agreements and evidence of consideration
Securities register and share certificates, if issued
Beneficial-ownership information and applicable REQ filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct incomplete minutes or registers by supplemental resolutions and entries. File overdue or amended REQ disclosures promptly and address any statutory late-filing penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish tax and payroll accounts as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec online services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain or confirm the corporation’s CRA business number and open applicable corporation income-tax, GST/HST, payroll, and import/export accounts. Register for Quebec corporation income tax, QST, source deductions, and employer accounts where thresholds or activities require them. Use the NEQ and incorporation documents to support registrations.
required_dossiers: Expected taxable supplies and payroll details, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct account information with the relevant tax authority and complete any overdue registration or return; assess applicable interest and penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industry-specific industrial licensing board applies to an app-growth, search-optimization, or localization agency. Business registration is handled by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; municipal authorities govern applicable premises and land-use requirements.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific operating or manufacturing permit is ordinarily required for the described professional services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l’Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not ordinarily subject to a project-specific environmental impact assessment or environmental authorization for a non-industrial office-based agency. Reassess if the business undertakes a separately regulated activity or site development.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No agency-specific wastewater, VOC, or industrial-waste thresholds ordinarily apply to office-based services. Any applicable municipal sewer, waste-management, and general environmental rules remain in force; regulated discharges or emissions require separate assessment and authorization.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No manufacturing or industrial clearance is ordinarily required. For leased or occupied premises, comply with applicable municipal occupancy and building requirements, Quebec fire-safety rules, and workplace obligations under the Act respecting occupational health and safety; obtain any required municipal occupancy or fire approvals for the specific premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal corporate income tax and GST/HST administration via the CRA Business Portal (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency); Revenu Québec (RQ) — provincial corporation tax, Quebec Sales Tax (QST), payroll source deductions, and Quebec enterprise registration via the Registraire des entreprises portal (registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca and revenuquebec.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Business Corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act (if federal) or the Quebec Business Corporations Act (if provincial) and obtain the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) from the Registraire des entreprises. Step 2: Register with the CRA for a 15-digit Business Number (BN) with program accounts: 'RC' for federal corporate income tax, 'RT' for GST/HST, 'RP' for payroll deduction, and 'RQ' or 'RM' for non-resident withholding where applicable. Step 3: Register with Revenu Québec for the QST account (required if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000) and, once the Ontario or Quebec payroll obligations arise, open source-deduction accounts. Step 4: A non-resident-owned corporation carrying on business in Canada must file federal T2 and Quebec CO-17 annual returns; GST/HST and QST registration is compulsory before invoicing Canadian clients unless the small-supplier threshold (CAD 30,000 worldwide) remains unmet.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Canadian-resident corporation is a separate person taxed on worldwide net income under federal Part I tax and Quebec Part I tax, with no pass-through or partnership look-through; a non-resident-owned corporation carrying on business in Quebec is also subject to Quebec and federal branch tax (Part XIV, 25% rate subject to treaty reduction) and branches into Quebec QST nexus as a registrant.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election; corporations are per se separate taxable entities for domestic purposes. Available elections relevant to the ASO/SEO localization agency: (i) functional-currency election under Income Tax Act (ITA) s.261 where the Canadian corporation computes income in USD; (ii) capital dividend account election under ITA s.83(2) for private corporations; (iii) section 85 rollover election on incorporation of an unincorporated business; (iv) GST/HST election under Excise Tax Act s.211 (nil consideration for closely related corporations); note that foreign hybrid-mismatch elections have no domestic force and ITA ss.18.4-18.6 automatically deny or recharacterize deductions on hybrid instruments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) at the federal level plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST) administered by Revenu Québec; combined Quebec GST/QST generally applies to taxable supplies of services, including ASO and SEO localization services, made in Quebec; exports of services to non-residents are generally zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated exports and capital property) before GST/HST and QST registration becomes mandatory; registrants may voluntarily register earlier, and a non-resident with a permanent establishment in Quebec or invoicing Canadian clients in respect of Quebec-based assets or services generally requires registration regardless of the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: CRA operates no real-time fiscal clearance, no API stamping mandate, and no mandatory e-invoicing at the federal level; EDI and PDF invoices are acceptable if retained in readable form. Revenu Québec has announced a phased mandatory B2B electronic-invoicing framework beginning from the 2025-2026 transition period for large enterprises, but as of the current compliance vintage no Quebec production mandate or central clearance stamping is in force; exporters must nevertheless preserve full digital audit trails, original billing metadata, and six-year retention records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada qualify for zero-rating under Excise Tax Act (ETA) Schedule VI Part V when exported by the supplier and substantiated by adequate evidence of export. Services are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI Part V s.7 when supplied to a non-resident recipient who is not registered for GST/HST and who does not acquire the service for use in a Canadian business; the service must not relate to Canadian real property, tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of supply, or an individual present in Canada. ASO campaign management, multilingual SEO localization, and App Store optimization delivered to a foreign app developer or offshore publisher normally satisfy the s.7 non-resident service test provided the supporting contract identifies the foreign recipient, the deliverables are performed outside a Canadian permanent establishment, and no Canadian property or Canadian-resident end-user is the direct subject matter.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A or authorized online export declaration filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System) for tangible goods exceeding the CRA/StatsCan reporting thresholds
Signed commercial invoice or executed service agreement naming the non-resident recipient and describing the offshore ASO/SEO localization deliverables
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / carrier cargo manifest for physical exports, or delivery and campaign performance records for digital services
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/PSP statements (SWIFT MT103, Wise B2B, Payoneer transaction reports) evidencing payment from abroad in foreign currency
Foreign customs entry documentation and any third-party verification (Google Play/App Store publisher records) demonstrating the export was completed outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day value is the standard tax-engine risk ordinal, while the legal retention rule is six years. CRA and Revenu Québec aggressively audit zero-rated export claims by ASO/SEO agencies; if the exporter cannot produce contemporaneous non-resident service evidence or proof of physical export, the zero rate is reversed retroactively, yielding GST/HST at 5% plus QST at 9.975%, statutory interest, and penalties. ETA s.280 imposes a gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the tax sought to be evaded; ETA s.327 creates summary and indictable offences with fines up to CAD 20,000 and imprisonment up to five years for fraudulent evasion; ITA s.163(2) adds a 50% penalty for false statements, and Revenu Québec applies parallel QST penalties. The normal CRA reassessment window is four years, extended to seven years for misrepresentation attributable to neglect, and unlimited for fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), Ottawa; Canada maintains a liberalized foreign-exchange administration regime with no dedicated exchange-control agency comparable to a SAFE-style authority. Bank supervision is vested in the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), while cross-border AML/reporting oversight is administered by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible across both current and capital account items; Canada has accepted the obligations of Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. There are no exchange-control restrictions on dividend, profit, interest, or royalty remittances, nor on capital repatriation. The operative frictions are fiscal rather than exchange-control based: Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%, treaty-reducible) on dividends and similar remittances to non-residents, plus FINTRAC reporting thresholds for cross-border currency movements, virtual-currency transfers, and large cash transactions generally exceeding CAD 10,000.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian law and Quebec regulation impose no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to repatriate export or service receipts. Exporters and cross-border service providers may retain foreign-currency proceeds indefinitely, manage them through domestic or foreign bank accounts, and hedge freely. Canadian-dollar income reporting and functional-currency tax elections are governed by the Income Tax Act, while Export Development Canada (EDC) provides trade finance and risk-mitigation support without exchange-control conditions.

Operating Account + Capital Call / Trust Account
Operating Account + International Business Centre Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High operational viability for Wise B2B and Payoneer as supplementary treasury and settlement rails, but legally constrained by their status as Money Service Businesses registered with FINTRAC rather than Schedule I/II Canadian chartered banks. Funds held on these platforms do not constitute CDIC-insured bank deposits; they are custodial or agent balances reconciled against partner-bank accounts. Recommended architecture: use Wise B2B for multi-currency vendor payouts, non-resident contractor settlement, and USD collection sub-accounts; use Payoneer for marketplace/ad-network receiving and disbursement; maintain the capital escrow, statutory records, and primary CAD liquidity with a Tier-1 domestic bank to satisfy OSFI expectations, audit requirements, and counterparty risk standards.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate requires directors of a CBCA/Quebec business corporation to appear physically in a branch. Major Canadian banks accept remote video KYC interviews for corporate onboarding where signatories and ultimate beneficial owners present valid government-issued identification. Non-resident directors are permissible but give rise to enhanced due diligence; banks typically require a Quebec Registraire des entreprises certificate of status, executed corporate resolutions, certified copies of passports, and either notarized or apostilled documentation supporting the corporate record. Remote opening is therefore feasible, but a recorded video interview with the economic owner and a verifiable Canadian operating address materially accelerate the underwriting decision.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner domiciled in a high-risk or offshore jurisdiction, or a multi-tier shareholding structure obscuring the control chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate organigram from the Canadian entity to each UBO; certified passport copies of all 25%+ owners; bank reference letters from each UBO's home institution; source-of-wealth statement; evidence of operational substance in Quebec including employee records, payroll, office lease, and client contracts; and an independent counsel opinion on the ownership structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: App Store and ad-network settlement flows arriving from diverse jurisdictions with platform-level payouts lacking standard invoice-level counterparty detail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master service agreements with each client; official payout reports from Apple, Google, Microsoft, and major ad-tech/demand-side platforms; invoice-level reconciliation ledger mapping platform transactions to bank credits; reviewed or audited financial statements; and a documented treasury policy governing multi-currency collections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Treasury flows touching crypto-asset conversions, digital-asset custodians, or PSP channel residuals that trigger unexplained-wire flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transaction trail from a licensed Canadian or foreign crypto custodian/PSP to the operating account; FINTRAC-compliant reporting evidence; a legal opinion on digital-asset tax characterization under the CRA framework; board resolution restricting crypto settlement to approved licensed intermediaries; and contemporaneous accounting entries demonstrating the business purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office flagged as a virtual office, formation-agent address, or shared co-working location rather than a substantive commercial premise.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec commercial lease or sublease; telecom, utilities, and property-insurance invoices in the corporate name; certified copies of the Registraire des entreprises registration showing a current physical address; notarized declaration of physical establishment; and a director/employee presence attestation supported by payroll or attendance records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire protocol: SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank instructions) remitted from the foreign shareholder to the Canadian operating or capital escrow account. Remittance purpose must state 'Foreign direct investment — share capital contribution' to align with Bank of Canada/Statistics Canada FDI classification. The foreign shareholder must file the applicable Investment Canada Act notification with Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) where a non-Canadian establishes a new Canadian business above the prescribed value thresholds; otherwise a simple post-establishment notification is required. The Canadian receiving bank attributes the purpose code, records beneficial ownership, and submits a Large Cash/Cross-Border Transaction Report to FINTRAC for transfers at or above CAD 10,000. The issuer must contemporaneously update the corporate share register, allocate contributed surplus, and preserve director resolutions authorizing the issuance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and trade settlements should use SWIFT MT103 for final irrevocable remittances, supported by invoice and contract references. Purchase-order-backed transactions may be structured through documentary commercial letters of credit initiated via SWIFT MT700 and amended via MT707, with document examination performed at the negotiating bank. Domestic CAD legs clear through Payments Canada's Lynx (LVTS) real-time gross settlement system, while USD legs settle over SWIFT/CHIPS rails. Wise B2B sub-accounts are cleared for vendor, contractor, and multi-currency payouts at reduced FX cost; Payoneer is used for ad-network and marketplace receiving/disbursement. All disbursements pass through a payment factory with invoice-level approval, three-way matching, and daily general-ledger reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla CAD/USD outright forward contracts with tenors up to 24 months executed with a Canadian Schedule I bank under ISDA/CSA or bilateral master trading agreements
Foreign exchange swaps (spot-forward or forward-forward) used for rolling short-term liquidity and balance-sheet currency matching
Cross-currency interest rate swaps matching CAD fixed-rate receipts against USD floating-rate obligations for long-term economic hedging
Covered FX options (purchased puts and calls only) with premium costs capitalized under the treasury policy; naked or written option positions are not permitted

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are technically available in the interbank market but are illiquid and economically unnecessary for CAD, which is fully convertible; onshore deliverable forwards are the preferred execution rail

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 12 online filing fee; persistent non-filing may result in compliance action and administrative dissolution or cancellation after statutory notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Updating Declaration under the Quebec Business Corporations Act or Quebec enterprise-registration rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within 30 days after the annual registration anniversary; confirm the entity-specific deadline shown in the enterprise register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or missing declarations may generate penalties, default status, collection measures, and cancellation or dissolution for persistent non-compliance; separate annual registration fees may apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada or Registraire des entreprises du Québec, according to the incorporation statute and registration status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirm with each annual return or annual updating declaration and update within the statutory period after any change, generally 15 days federally and 30 days in Quebec.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties, filing rejection or default status, and possible dissolution or cancellation for continuing non-compliance; directors and officers may face personal statutory penalties for inaccurate information.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general revenue, asset, or employee threshold applies to a private corporation. An independent auditor is generally required unless a valid shareholder waiver is available under the applicable federal or Quebec corporate statute; public or distributing corporations generally cannot rely on the private-company waiver.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Generally Accepted Accounting Principles. Private enterprises generally use Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); publicly accountable enterprises use IFRS. Tax filings must comply with Canadian federal and Quebec tax rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Maintain current information on individuals with significant control or ultimate beneficiaries, including ownership, control, and identifying details. Confirm the information with the applicable annual filing and update the register and government record within the prescribed change-notification period.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control or Ultimate Beneficiaries
Share transfer register and securities register
Minute book containing shareholder and director resolutions and meeting minutes
Articles, by-laws, certificates, registers, and filed corporate returns

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250-1,200 per year, depending on whether the provider supplies only a registered office or also corporate secretarial and filing services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000-15,000 for a straightforward private corporation; higher fees apply for complex transactions, consolidation, regulated activities, or IFRS reporting
